# Data Frames

```{r}
crashes_by_day = c(2020, 2241, 2327, 2285, 2380, 1866, 1664)
names(crashes_by_day) = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu",
                          "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")

crashes_df = tibble::tibble(
  day     = names(crashes_by_day),
  crashes = crashes_by_day,
  busy    = crashes_by_day > 2000
)
crashes_df

dplyr::glimpse(crashes_df) #equivalent of str() but prints neater
```

# Examining the Job Ad
```{r}
job = list(
  title   = "Research Data Scientist, Magic Eye",
  company = "Google",
  salary  = list(min = 147000, max = 210000)
)
dplyr::glimpse(job)


# 1. The company name
company_name = job$
  

# 2. Max salary
max_salary = job$salary$max

# 3. Max salary again; using only [[]]
job[[3]][[2]]

# 4. The names of the elements in job
names(job)
```

## Sub-setting

## Vectors

- You can subset by position or by name if it is a named vector;
- You can also pass a vector for sub-setting the vector

```{r}
crashes_by_day = c(2020, 2241, 2327, 2285, 2380, 1866, 1664)
names(crashes_by_day) = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu",
                          "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")
crashes_by_day[2:4]
crashes_by_day[c('Mon', 'Fri')]
```
```{r jobs}
oh_jobs = readr::read_csv(
  file = https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?bgcolor=%23ebf3fb&chart_type=line&drp=0&fo=open%20sans&graph_bgcolor=%23ffffff&height=450&mode=fred&recession_bars=on&txtcolor=%23444444&ts=12&tts=12&width=1320&nt=0&thu=0&trc=0&show_legend=yes&show_axis_titles=yes&show_tooltip=yes&id=IHLIDXUSOH&scale=left&cosd=2021-08-21&coed=2026-08-28&line_color=%230073e6&link_values=false&line_style=solid&mark_type=none&mw=3&lw=3&ost=-99999&oet=99999&mma=0&fml=a&fq=Daily%2C%207-Day&fam=avg&fgst=lin&fgsnd=2020-02-01&line_index=1&transformation=lin&vintage_date=2026-09-02&revision_date=2026-09-02&nd=2020-02-01)
```

## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
